401911642.summary: Nakamura's experience and finish rate favor him, but the -350 price is steep for a 37-year-old against a younger, longer opponent with recent KO power.
reasons: Nakamura is 8-1 with five straight wins and finishes most opponents (7 KOs, 1 sub), while Schmid is 4-3 with inconsistent results and recent KO loss to Rahiki
Nine-year age gap and Nakamura's ex-fight status suggest better ring IQ and durability despite being older
Schmid is taller and longer but has been finished by KO twice; Nakamura's southpaw stance and 70-inch reach give him tooling advantage at featherweight
The -350 line reflects heavy chalk; while justified by record, it leaves little margin and makes moneyline a poor parlay piece

401928111.summary: Suarez's wrestling and submission prowess should control Jandiroba's grappling, but Jandiroba's submission defense and decision-heavy recent record make this closer than the -175 price suggests.
reasons: Suarez 13-1 record and wrestling base favored against Jandiroba's 23-4, but both fighters' recent wins come via decision not finishes
Jandiroba's 14 submission wins and BJJ specialization mean this is not a one-dimensional matchup; age 38 and recent decision streak suggest she avoids exchanges
Moneyline -175 overweights Suarez given Jandiroba's legitimate submission threat and recent competitive performances against top opposition; not a confident par

401928113.summary: Fernando's recent finishing streak and reach advantage favor him, but Elekana's submission prowess and experience offer intrigue; the line slightly overvalues Fernando's -258 for a three-round main card fight with variance.
reasons: Fernando 5-0 recent with 3 straight TKO finishes in rounds 1-3; Elekana 3-2 recent with wins by submission showing different skill set
Fernando's 80.5" reach gives 3" advantage for striking; both same height but Fernando's orthodox stance and KO rate (8-14 record) suggest more consistent power
Elekana's loss to Aslan by decision and sub loss to recent opponent show vulnerability to pressure; Fernando has not been finished in 17 fights
Three-round format favors Fernando's aggressive finisher style; -258 is steep for a non-title fight without injury reports or major skill gap

401928115.summary: Silva's superior grappling and recent decision consistency favor her, but Fernandes is older, longer, and the price doesn't fully justify the pick given both fighters' inconsistency.
reasons: Silva's last three fights all went to decision; Fernandes got KO'd in her last outing, suggesting vulnerability to volume striking
Silva reaches 67 inches with BJJ base against a 66-inch striker without submission threat; grappling advantage in tight matchup
Moneyline at -160 undervalues the risk; both fighters show volatile records and neither is a heavy favorite worthy of parlays

401928116.summary: Milošević's perfect recent form, significant reach advantage, and explosive finishing power overcome Cachoeira's experience, but the -440 price is too steep for parlay construction.
reasons: Milošević is 5-0 in last five with four finishes; Cachoeira is 1-4 with three recent KO/sub losses showing vulnerability to power and grappling
Seven-inch reach advantage (67 vs 65) favors Milošević's ability to control range and land cleanly
Milošević averages 4 KO wins to 2 subs; Cachoeira at 38 and coming off submission losses to grapplers is susceptible to early strikes
Odds reflect reality: -440 is appropriate for a striker with hot hands facing a declining, chinny opponent, making it poor value in multiples

401928117.summary: Ko's recent form and decision-heavy record favor him, but Turman's KO power and long layoff create uncertainty that the -550 price does not adequately reflect.
reasons: Ko is 4-1 in last five with three straight decisions; Turman is 2-3 in last five with a 1064-day layoff creating rust risk
Ko wins 7 of 13 by decision versus Turman's 6 of 18; Ko's southpaw stance and recent activity suggest a technical points victory
The -550 moneyline overvalues Ko as a heavy favorite given Turman's KO finishing ability (4 KOs in 18 wins) and Ko's limited finish rate (6 KOs, 0 subs in 13 wi
Ko's lone recent loss was a decision to Jean-Paul Lebosnoyani, showing vulnerability to active opponents; Turman can pressure effectively

401928118.summary: Henrique's youth, size, recent activity and perfect record at -185 justify the favorite role, but the price lacks margin given Parsons' finishing power and recent KO streak.
reasons: Henrique is 11 years younger with 10-inch reach advantage, elite camp pedigree, and perfect recent form against live opponents
Parsons' 1198-day layoff is substantial; while he returned with two KOs, ring rust in a skill matchup favors the active fighter
Henrique 6-0 by KO or decision with no subs; Parsons heavy on KO (7 of 9 wins) but split decision losses suggest vulnerable wrestling defense that Henrique may
Moneyline at -185 prices in little edge; this is a live underdog situation where Parsons' power and experience present real upset value

401928119.summary: Smith's youth, undefeated record, and recent finishing power favor him, but Grant's experience and submission defense create enough uncertainty to avoid heavy favorites in parlays.
reasons: Smith is 10-1 with five straight wins including recent KO and submission finishes; Grant is 40 with mixed recent results and a submission loss to Jourdain just
Smith's 71-inch reach and finishing rate (7 of 10 wins by KO/sub) give him multiple paths to victory against a 40-year-old primarily winning by decision
The moneyline price of -225 is moderate for a fighter this young facing a 40-year-old; not steep enough to risk in parlays where Grant's grappling and experienc

401928120.summary: Magomedov's undefeated record, finish-heavy style, and slight reach advantage make him the technical pick, but Delano's recent form and experience warrant respect; the moneyline prices are too tight for parlay confidence.
reasons: Magomedov is 11-0 with 11 of 11 wins by finish (5 KO, 6 sub) vs Delano's mixed record and decision-heavy wins (8 of 17 wins)
Delano's recent three wins are all decisions over modest competition, suggesting potential stylistic vulnerability to aggressive finishers
Moneylines nearly identical despite Magomedov's undefeated status and superior finish rate signals market uncertainty; neither side is a parlay lock

401932011.summary: Kondratavičius is a rising prospect with superior athleticism and finish rate facing a declining 35-year-old coming off two straight KO losses, but the -290 price is steep for a parlay piece given middleweight volatility.
reasons: Kondratavičius 9-1 with 4 straight wins and 67% KO rate versus Petroski 13-7 with 2 KOs in last 5 fights and back-to-back first and second round KO losses
Five year age gap (27 vs 35) combined with Petroski's recent concussive trauma suggests chinability and durability concerns for the older fighter
Kondratavičius has 2 inch reach advantage and Orthodox stance against Petroski's Switch stance; 225 days rest suggests peak readiness
Moneyline price of -290 requires sub-26% knockout risk for sound parlay construction; middleweight and Petroski's defensive issues make that unrealistic

401932012.summary: Degli's dominant recent form, finishing power, and stylistic advantages over Raposo support the favourite, but the -245 line is steep for a preliminary flyweight bout with inherent variance.
reasons: Degli is 5-0 in last five with three straight finishes; Raposo is 2-3 in last five with only decisions in wins
Degli's 9 KO wins and aggressive Vale Top Team style match up well against Raposo's submission-heavy record (3 of 7 wins) and recent decision tendency
Degli's reach advantage (67 vs 64.5 inches) and orthodox stance give him spatial control against switch stance Raposo
Raposo's sole KO loss and Degli's finishing rate (14 of 18 wins) suggest KO is Degli's highest-probability path

401932715.summary: Walker's recent KO streak and significant reach advantage make him the value pick, but his inconsistency, age, and Cortes Acosta's recent decision losses (not finishes) to elite competition create enough uncertainty to avoid parlay exposure.
reasons: Walker has won 2 of last 3 fights by KO including R1 finish over Parkin; Cortes Acosta has lost last 2 to better ranked opponents via decision only, suggesting
Walker's 4-inch reach advantage (82 vs 78) and striker profile favor him in the striking exchanges that heavy favorites need to control
Walker's 23-10 record shows volatility at 34 years old, and the +170 price compensates for that unreliability better than backing the -190 favorite
Both fighters are strikers with recent decision losses, reducing confidence in either as a parlay piece; Cortes Acosta's -190 lacks the dominant finish rate nee
